findings.issue: The CLI's default "strict": true is missing, and angularCompilerOptions lacks strictTemplates, so template and type errors compile silently.
findings.suggestion: Re-enable strict mode and strictTemplates; the code is already written in a strict-friendly style, so this should be cheap.

findings.issue: A rejected /_data fetch fails the route resolver, which cancels client-side navigation with no user-visible error state.
findings.suggestion: Either catch and render an error/not-found view, or add a router-level error handler that surfaces the failure.

findings.issue: The browser page-data cache checks TTL on read but never evicts expired entries, so it grows unbounded over a long session (one entry per distinct path, including per-game Pokémon pages).
findings.suggestion: Delete expired entries on read, or cap the map like the server's api-client does.

findings.issue: linkedSignal computation reads mutable instance state (this.pushedQ), a non-reactive dependency; and a pending debounce timer can fire after browser Back and re-push the typed q over the restored URL.
findings.suggestion: Track the pushed value in the signal itself (e.g. store {q, pushed} in one linkedSignal) and cancel the timer when the URL changes externally.

findings.issue: TeamVM.coverage is computed server-side and shipped in every /_data/team response, but the client never reads it (team-page recomputes from attackTypes + members).
findings.suggestion: Remove coverage from TeamVM, or have the component use vm.coverage and recompute only after local mutations.

findings.issue: Routes and loaders are coupled by stringly-typed page-data paths ('/home', '/pokemon/<name>?game=...'); a typo or drift fails only at runtime as Not Found.
findings.suggestion: Derive the path strings from a single shared constant/union type, or unit-test the resolver-to-loader mapping (the format.spec.ts suite is the only test today).

findings.issue: Hand-rolled scroll restoration via Scroll events, previous-URL diffing and afterNextRender reimplements router functionality; subtle behavior (popstate position, anchor, page-change top) lives in one subscription.
findings.suggestion: Keep it, but extract the previous/changedPage logic into a named helper or add the one focused test this file most deserves.

findings.issue: All 641 lines of CSS, including per-component styles (pokemon-card, move-table, team-list), live in one global stylesheet.
findings.suggestion: Consider component-scoped styles for the shared components at least; the anyComponentStyle budget in angular.json already anticipates them.

findings.issue: Uses @Injectable() while the rest of the app uses the now-stable @Service().
findings.suggestion: Either switch to @Service({autoProvided: false}) for consistency, or note why the classic decorator is kept for manually-provided classes.

summary: A notably well-architected Angular 22 SSR app: resolvers feeding input-bound view models, a clean server-only BFF with TransferState hydration parity, stable v22 idioms (@Service, linkedSignal, zoneless-friendly signals) throughout. The team feature integrates cleanly via a cookie-backed store that both the server renderer and the browser read. I'd merge after one small round: restore strict/strictTemplates, evict the client cache, remove the dead TeamVM.coverage field, and simplify the search-input sync trick.
